why: the mutual-exclusion latch a multi-threaded executor sets while one of the group's callbacks runs. rclcpp's `CallbackGroupType` is a CONCURRENCY policy -- `MutuallyExclusive` or `Reentrant` -- and it only means anything to a multi-threaded executor deciding whether two callbacks from one group may run at once. RFC-0002 puts one executor on one RTOS task with non-preemptive run-to-completion dispatch, so every group is mutually exclusive by construction and `Reentrant` is unrepresentable: there is no second thread to be reentrant from. The axis our group carries instead is a NAME that `system.toml` maps to a scheduling tier (RFC-0047, RFC-0079) -- the thing a mixed-criticality image actually needs from grouping. `automatically_add_to_executor_with_node` (rclcpp's second constructor argument) is meaningless for the same reason as `cpp:Executor::add_node`.
